comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body: Possible second shape, same evening: a worker's Claude Code pane showed a box above its prompt reading '✦ Heads up · The main agent concluded ... 1: Learn more  2: Knew this already  0: Dismiss'. It did not hold a wake: a post to that pane rang at once while the box was on screen (or had just gone). So it is not established that every such box holds wakes; the feedback-draft box did, for 30 minutes. Record each with its version.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Seen 2026-10-16, Muster 0.16.0, the integrator's own Claude Code pane on the laptop. After a session drafted a bug report with Claude Code's feedback tool, the harness drew a box just above the prompt and left it there:

    ╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
    │ ✻ Bug report drafted: Spawned five parallel Opus ... │
    │ │ - What happened: ...                               │
    │ 1 to review · 2 to send · 0 to dismiss               │
    ╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
    ───────────────────────────────────── MUSTER ─
    ❯

From the moment its turn ended (01:35:41Z) the doorbell logged `msg.ring.waits why="its screen is not its prompt"` on every look, 536 times over 30 minutes, while the pane read `done`. Two wakes from another integrator were held, and each stall notice said "something typed in its prompt, or a menu over it".

Holding was right: the box takes digits, so a wake typed there could press "2 to send" and submit a bug report the person had not approved. What was wrong is the explanation, and that nothing tells the person, whose answer is the only way out.

Ruled out: the footer's "2 shells, 1 monitor" (background tasks). The first held look came before any were running.

What would help: a rule in `claude.toml` that recognises the box as covering the prompt (the way a menu or viewer is, without changing the agent's state), so the doorbell's typed reason (since the stall-notice change on this branch, `Unseen::Covered`) names it. Recording the screen under corpus/claude-code-<version>/ first, with the version noted. Whether a box like this should also notify the human is worth deciding with it, since the wake waits on them.
title: A wake held behind Claude Code's feedback-draft box is blamed on a draft, and no rule knows the box
